definitions.explanation: A portion cut from something larger.
A piece of fabric or material.
Used as a counter for slices or pieces.

examples.japanese: ケーキを{一切|ひときれ}{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate a slice of cake.

examples.japanese: {刺身|さしみ}を{一切|ひときれ}ください。
チーズの{小|ちい}さな{切|き}れを{何枚|なんまい}か{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought several small pieces of cheese.
To wipe with a piece of cloth.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{着物|きもの}の{切|き}れを{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: I collect scraps of old kimono fabric.

examples.japanese: この{切|き}れは{何|なに}の{布|ぬの}ですか。
examples.english: What kind of cloth is this piece?

examples.japanese: パンを{二切|ふたきれ}ください。
{魚|さかな}を{四切|よんきれ}に{切|き}って、{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I cut the fish into four pieces and grilled them.

notes:
{切|き}れ is derived from {切|き}る (to cut).

AS NOUN:
- {一切|ひときれ} (one slice/piece)
- {布|ぬの}{切|き}れ (piece of cloth)
- {端|は}{切|ぎ}れ (scrap, remnant)

AS COUNTER:
- {一切|ひときれ}、{二切|ふたきれ}、{三切|さんきれ} (one, two, three slices)

COMMON ITEMS:
- パン{一切|ひときれ} (a slice of bread)
- {肉|にく}{一切|ひときれ} (a piece of meat)
- {魚|さかな}{一切|ひときれ} (a piece of fish)
